pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql; test AC-1 checks all existing rows are 0 and CHECK rejects 2.
test AC-2 asserts ★ only on the starred item.
test AC-3 stars 3 and 1, expects id order.
test AC-5 checks exact links in both views.
test AC-6 checks 400 and no <li> for several values.
routes.json contains /?show=starred; test AC-7 asserts it.

findings.what: The last commit 'Follow-up edits' deletes the 'Empty table' state test (empty message 'No items yet.' plus the Starred only link). The spec's States table has an 'Empty table' row, so that row now has no test. The PR also claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', which is false. A stray blank line is left behind.
findings.fix:
Restore the Empty table test (DELETE FROM items, then check the empty list, '

No items yet.

' and the 'Starred only' link), and remove the extra blank line.

findings.what: The body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the follow-up commit deleted a test. It also says test/starred.test.js covers 'each state', which is no longer true.
findings.fix: Correct the claims once the test is restored.

lenses.note: The behaviour matches the spec, decisions are followed, and no extra scope was added. The relaxed traffic route check is needed for AC-7 and is disclosed.
All 7 ACs are named by tests. The Empty table state row lost its test in the last commit.
Tests are behavioural. The Empty table test was deleted without spec justification. I could not run the suite here, so CI should cover that.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The change adds no other docs.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, the SQL is constant, and titles are escaped. No defects found.
The show value is only checked against a fixed allowlist and never put into SQL or HTML. The fragment and space checks in the route validator are still enforced and tested.
The page has no CSS or interaction work. Only a link and a ★ prefix were added, so I treated this as having no UI to review.
There is no browser flow. The change is covered by worker tests only.
The 'none deleted' claim is false, and the 'each state' claim is no longer accurate.
